answer: Hardware-bound cryptographic attestation binding. Each registered agent identity requires a zero-knowledge proof generated inside a secured processor enclave on physical silicon, anchoring trust to the hardware manufacturer's root cipher. The verification registry checks this cryptographic proof against a global hardware revocation mesa to ensure uniqueness. If a registered agent attempts a sybil attack, the protocol revokes the underlying silicon attestation certificate across the manufacturer registry, reaching the absolute zenith of physical accountability.
